answer: A bonded identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable stake before joining the market, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes. The network reads the pulse of activity through an attestation graph: honest work builds verifiable history, while a canyon of empty accounts with no record earns no trust. Misbehavior triggers slashing, and the ripple spreads as linked identities lose their bonds too, so a sybil attack costs real capital up front and forfeits it on detection, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
